Grant access only to the intended users after the setup checks, using a feature-scoped permission set. ... The Salesforce admin owns the selected endpoint and model configuration, which users cannot edit from the bot.

A completion from an abandoned view cannot update a replacement view or another user's view. ... No new persistent telemetry, per-user history or bot audit system. Platform and provider traces follow their own access and retention settings.
A single Apex callout is sufficient for the foreground interaction. ... The stateless foreground design has no worker, broker or persisted operation record.
verdicts.missing: The callout restrictions (no callout from a trigger, no callout after uncommitted DML) are not stated, and the design is a synchronous foreground callout rather than Queueable/future/batch; a builder must still decide how those constraints are respected.

verdicts.quote: Use a modern Named Credential ... and a Custom authentication External Credential with a named principal. ... Ship credential metadata without the secret. ... Application diagnostics omit credentials
The Salesforce synchronous ceilings include 100 callouts and 120 seconds cumulative callout timeout per transaction, with a 6 MB callout payload limit that also counts towards heap.
verdicts.missing: The CPU time limit and the heap limit's own value are not named.

verdicts.quote: At the integration boundary exercise each error class with controlled responses, assert outbound counts and sanitized outcomes
verdicts.missing: No statement that Apex tests cannot make real callouts or that a mock callout implementation (HttpCalloutMock) is required.

verdicts.quote: Use a modern Named Credential targeting the approved xAI HTTPS base URL

The component uses a non-cacheable imperative Apex entry point. ... There is no incremental record state, cache invalidation, callback, subscription or durable recovery because this interaction is a fresh request/response.
verdicts.missing: The spec relies on the imperative call returning the answer inline; no platform event, CDC, polled status field or LMS mechanism is defined.

verdicts.quote: One outbound attempt at most per admitted send. ... No automatic resend, and a manual resend is a fresh request. ... Attempts to repeat Send while pending produce no second call.
Selected prompt and output limits, timeout, expected concurrent load and any spend ceiling remain unresolved
verdicts.missing: No concurrency or queue limit is named, and the outcome for a request that cannot be admitted because of concurrency is not stated.

verdicts.missing: Timeout and 5xx share one outcome rather than distinct ones; other 4xx refusals (e.g. 400) are not assigned an outcome.
